title: Grappling hooks that work: click to throw, equipped hook for F, reliable latch on natural terrain/platforms/trees, per-hook heads and chains
player_outcome: Hooks latch onto natural slopes, platforms and trees and stay latched. You can throw the held hook with a click or the equipped hook with F. Every hook looks like itself: gem hooks with gem chains, and the Ivy Whip as a green vine.
design: Verified: ItemAction.Grapple is parsed (ItemUseTable.cs:159) but Use() has no branch. The attach check nudges 5 cm into a voxel cell (PlayerController.Grapple.cs:106-111) and releases on smoothed terrain. The ray excludes PlatformLayer (:64). There is one generic claw/chain for every hook (GrappleVisual.cs).
ItemUseSystem: ItemAction.Grapple raises GrappleRequested(p, ItemUseInfo) and returns a new UseOutcome.Grappled. WorldLauncher wires it to PlayerController.FireHook(info.Grapple).
BestHook: the Misc hook slot first (P3-16), else the strongest in the backpack (Terraria fallback).

FireHook ray mask adds PlatformLayer and ObjectLayer. On hit, compute an anchor: the solid cell at hit − normal·0.1, else the nearest solid cell or tile object in the 3×3×3 around CellAt(hit). Store _hookAnchorCell or _hookAnchorObject.
Attached state re-validates only that anchor, every 10 frames; it releases only when the anchor is air or the object is gone.
GrappleParams: Head (item id; default the hook item) and Chain ('links' | 'vine' | 'gem').
GrappleVisual draws the head with PropLibrary.Model(ItemModel(head)) oriented along the chain, and the chain with ChainStrip (links), a twisted green strip (vine) or gem-coloured glowing links (gem).
Remove the keybind hint from the grappling_hook description; tooltips/hints are P2.
files_modify: game/Player/PlayerController.Grapple.cs — equipped hook, anchor search, throttled check, platform/object mask
game/Player/GrappleVisual.cs — head model and chain styles
data_changes: mobility.json: amethyst..diamond hooks chain 'gem'; ivy_whip chain 'vine'; grappling_hook and dual_hook chain 'links'; grappling_hook description without '(press F to throw)'
tests: ItemUseTests: using a held grappling_hook raises GrappleRequested
Smoke movement.cmds (click throw): 'wield grappling_hook' / 'aim 0 1 0' / 'hold use_primary 0.05' / 'wait 0.2' / 'assert player.hook >= 1'
Smoke movement.cmds (irregular ceiling): add a stepped ceiling with setblock at y 15/16/17, aim 0.3 1 0, hold grapple 0.05, wait 1.5, 'assert player.hook == 2'
Smoke movement.cmds (platform): place a wood platform row overhead, hold grapple, 'assert player.hook == 2'
verification: Manual lavapipe run on a natural hillside: the hook stays latched
risks: If P1 already reworked the grapple, merge the anchor logic instead of duplicating it.
Platform tiles may be crisp blocks vs objects; check both paths.
